Yes. With a 1:15 wrap, the Wednesday evening return is safe. I would book the Monday SFO-DEN-OMA option arriving about 6:15, the Wednesday OMA-DEN-SFO return after 5:30, a compact car at OMA, and the riverfront/Old Market hotel we shortlisted.

Booked. Flights are SFO-DEN-OMA Monday afternoon, arriving 6:14 p.m., and OMA-DEN-SFO Wednesday evening, arriving SFO 9:28 p.m. Compact rental is reserved at OMA. Hotel is Cambria Omaha Downtown/Riverfront, refundable, with paid onsite parking, strong guest feedback, and easy Old Market dinner access. Room note added for coffee maker and mini-fridge. Window seats selected on the available segments.
Good. What does the agenda look like now?

Tight version: Monday noon case delivery with warehouse signature, Monday 7:30 riverfront dinner, Tuesday 1:00-4:00 distributor operator training, Wednesday 7:30 municipal demo, 10:45 ride-along and debrief, leave the site by 1:15 for OMA.

messages.content: New one: South Texas coastal utility. They want me in Corpus for a Tuesday 6:00 a.m. plant walkdown and a Wednesday afternoon city staff briefing. Possible procurement meeting Thursday morning. Can you build flight, car, and hotel options?
I can. Are you targeting the week of September 14, and should I start with SFO only or compare SJC/OAK too?

Week of September 14. Start with SFO, but show me SJC only if it is materially cleaner. I need Monday travel, probably into Corpus Christi, but include San Antonio as a fallback if the small-airport connections look fragile.

For Monday into Corpus Christi, there are three workable shapes. Best schedule: SFO-DFW-CRP, departing 9:45 a.m. and arriving about 5:35 p.m., with a 70-minute Dallas connection. Later departure: SFO-IAH-CRP around noon, arriving about 7:55 p.m., with a more comfortable Houston connection. Late option: SFO-IAH-CRP after 1:00 p.m., arriving closer to 8:45 p.m.; I would avoid that unless prep is light.
Arrival at 8:45 is too late with a 6 a.m. walkdown. Noon through Houston might be okay. What about San Antonio?

San Antonio is a real fallback, not my first pick. You can get to SAT around 6:00-6:30 p.m., then it is roughly 2 hours 15 minutes to Corpus if traffic behaves. With rental pickup and a stop, you are likely at the hotel around 9:15. It avoids the CRP last leg but adds a long night drive before an early plant entry.
Agreed. Keep SAT in the notes, not the lead plan. I’d rather protect the plant start than be strict about a later departure.

Then I would rank them this way: 1, SFO-DFW-CRP arriving 5:35 if you want the strongest Tuesday buffer; 2, SFO-IAH-CRP arriving 7:55 if the later departure matters; 3, San Antonio only if Corpus fares or connection times fall apart. All are one-stop except the SAT drive piece.
Car should handle a plant road if it rains. Not a huge vehicle, though.

Compact SUV at CRP is the clean fit. It keeps the rental counter simple, handles wet gravel better than a sedan, and is not overkill. From SAT, the same class works, but the one-way and longer drive make it less attractive.
Hotel comparison: one near the airport or plant, and one bayfront. Quality matters. I don’t want a marginal airport hotel just because it saves ten minutes.

Airport/plant-side option: Fairfield Inn & Suites Corpus Christi Central, about 8-12 minutes from the plant area, guest rating around 4.3, free parking, breakfast, in-room coffee and fridge, but dinner is mostly a short drive. Bayfront option: Residence Inn Corpus Christi Downtown, around 18-22 minutes to the plant at that hour, guest rating around 4.4, paid onsite parking, larger rooms with fridge/coffee setup, and easy walking dinner options.
How early would I need to leave the bayfront hotel Tuesday?

For a 6:00 a.m. gate time, I would leave by 5:15 from the bayfront hotel. That gives room for a badge delay, a wrong gate, or a slow security check-in. From the airport-side hotel, 5:30 would probably be enough.
The bayfront dinner access is useful if I’m working slides Monday night. Any parking concern there?

Residence Inn has onsite paid parking, not street-only. It is easier than hunting for a public garage, and a compact SUV should be fine. The airport-side hotel has free parking, so the trade-off is basically ten minutes closer and cheaper parking versus better evening logistics downtown.
If the Thursday procurement meeting happens, can we avoid rebuilding the whole trip?

Yes. I’d price the outbound with a Thursday-capable return in mind and hold the hotel on a refundable three-night stay, Monday through Wednesday. If procurement is canceled, you can either switch to a Wednesday evening return or trim the third hotel night before the cancellation deadline.
Don’t book yet. Parts are still the open variable. If the chemical feed parts miss the shipment, I may push the whole thing a week.
Understood. I’ll keep it as a working shortlist, not a booking queue. The parts status should drive whether we ticket at all.
Send me the short version with what you would hold.

Short version: hold SFO-DFW-CRP Monday if Tuesday buffer is most important; acceptable backup is the noon SFO-IAH-CRP if you want the later departure and still arrive before 8. Reserve a compact SUV at CRP. Hotel best fit is Residence Inn Corpus Christi Downtown on a refundable Monday-Wednesday stay; airport-side Fairfield is the practical backup if plant proximity beats dinner access. Keep San Antonio as ask-before-booking only. Open items: parts onsite, Thursday procurement decision, and the hotel cancellation deadline.
